items.title: Brushing Scams: Why Random Packages Are Showing Up at Your Door
items.summary: A package shows up on your porch you never ordered. The FTC warned on August 20 that this is a "brushing" scam — sellers send you free junk using your name so they can post a fake five-star review in your name. Some packages include QR codes that lead to fake websites designed to steal your information. If you receive a package you did not order, do not scan any codes inside. Check your online accounts for unfamiliar orders and report it free at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

items.title: CISA Flags 4 Actively Exploited Flaws — Update Your Mac and Windows Now
items.summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added four new actively exploited vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on August 18. Two affect Apple Macs and two affect Windows. Update macOS at System Settings > General > Software Update and Windows at Settings > Windows Update tonight.

items.title: Fake Bill-Payment Websites Are Tricking You Through Search Ads
items.summary: The FTC just warned that scammers are buying fake ads at the top of Google and Bing that look like your electric company, insurance provider, or bank. You search for "pay my light bill," click the first result, enter your account number and card, and the money goes to a crook instead of your real company. Always scroll past the ads and look for the official web address you already know — or call the number on your paper bill. Report fraud at ReportFraud.ftc.gov. (Source: FTC.gov, August 17, 2026)

items.title: Stop Windows from begging you to buy Microsoft 365 — turn off the subscription nag screens
items.summary: Press the Windows key, type **Notifications** and press Enter. Scroll down and turn off notifications from **Microsoft 365 (Office)** and **Get Help**. That kills the pop-ups permanently — takes 30 seconds.

items.title: Microsoft Edge Browser Security Update — Check Yours in 30 Seconds Free
items.summary: Microsoft pushed a fresh security patch to Edge this week that closes several vulnerabilities attackers are actively exploiting through malicious websites. If your Edge browser is out of date, simply visiting the wrong page could let someone run code on your computer. Here's the fix — it's free and takes 30 seconds: open Microsoft Edge, click the three dots in the top right corner, choose Help and feedback, then About Microsoft Edge. The browser will show your current version and update automatically if it's not current. I do this check on every computer that comes into the shop, and I'm always surprised how many are months behind. Don't be one of them — check it now. (Source: Microsoft Security Response Center, August 2026)

items.title: Healthcare Company CareCloud Confirms Data Breach Affecting 3.7 Million Patients
items.summary: Healthcare technology company CareCloud confirmed a massive data breach that exposed personal information of 3.7 million patients, according to a report by BleepingComputer on August 19, 2026. If you or a family member received care from a medical provider that uses CareCloud systems, your name, contact details, and health-related information may have been compromised. Here's what to do right now: call your healthcare provider's office and ask if they use CareCloud, then place a free fraud alert on your credit reports by calling Equifax at 1-800-525-6285, Experian at 1-888-397-3742, or TransUnion at 1-800-680-7289.

items.title: Government warns ransomware gangs are targeting Windows computers right now — Windows Update keeps you safe
items.summary: CISA (the government's cybersecurity agency) confirmed that ransomware gangs are actively using a Windows flaw to take full control of computers. Open Settings, click Windows Update, and click "Check for updates" — it takes 2 minutes and keeps you safe.
